option.counterfactual: The set of attainable increments is empty because bounded increasing sequences in the specified finite AW*-factors always have least upper bounds.
option.approach: Investigate whether completeness in the quasitrace metric, together with an appropriate convergence theorem for bounded increasing sequences, yields a least upper bound in the algebra.

judge.reason: It makes the definite claim that the attainable-increment set is empty, which is exactly the answer already proposed in e1.

options.counterfactual: Finite AW*-factors are not known to be monotone sequentially complete, so that assertion cannot currently justify an answer to this problem.
options.approach: Audit the precise completeness theorem and distinguish completeness of the projection lattice, completeness in a quasitrace metric, and monotone sequential completeness. Identify the additional convergence statement needed to pass from metric completeness to a least upper bound.

options.counterfactual: There exists a witness with increment exactly one half, despite the restrictions imposed by faithfulness and the order bounds.
options.approach: Verify the witness against every defining condition, particularly the matrix extension of the quasitrace and the absence of a least upper bound. Then use scalar rescaling and the universal upper bound to determine the entire set.

options.counterfactual: The set is empty because bounded positive partial sums force their individual quasitrace values to tend to zero, even without assuming that bounded increasing sequences have suprema.
options.approach: Reduce the assertion to projections by taking fixed spectral cutoffs of the positive increments. Seek a packing theorem ruling out infinitely many projections of uniformly positive quasitrace whose partial sums are bounded.
